PullRequest.Title: sessions: make opening and reloading large Agent Host chats responsive
PullRequest.Body:

Follow-up to #341322 (round 2). A 1,157-request Agent Host chat ("Move chats") in the Agents window was slow to open, scroll and reload, and the renderer froze.

## Results

Median of 5 cold runs per build, local renderer traces.

| Area | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Open: time to idle | 11.1s | 7.0s |
| Open: long-task time | 7.1s | 2.7s |
| Open: `_resolvePath` waves | 5.1s | 1.0s |
| Scrollbar drag CPU per step | 90ms | 50ms |
| Drag long tasks | 170 | 40 |
| Sticky-scroll code per drag | 5.2s | 0.57s |
| `getItems`/`isHiddenFromTranscript` scan per drag | 3.6s | <1ms |

Window reload, from user traces:

| Area | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Session registration task | 3,516ms freeze | 197ms |
| 71MB default-chat snapshot pulled by list rows | 704ms | gone |
| Restore waiting behind long tasks | 3.58s | ~0.42s |
| Reload → chat rendered | 10.07s | 3.88s (small chat) / 5.2–5.8s (Move chats) |

"Not responding" was not observed after the fixes.

## Changes

- **Scrolling**
  - Customization path cache.
  - Sticky-scroll ranges measured once per animation frame.
  - `ChatViewModel.getItems()` cached and readonly; `response.request` index hint.
- **Opening**
  - Customization resolution moved off the click and made progressive, in idle slices.
  - Progress bar after 100ms.
  - `ChatGroupView`/`ChatView` reused across single-group session switches, keeping the view attached while rebinding.
  - List rerenders deferred while the list is detached or zero-height.
- **Reload**
  - Remote history restore uses fixed 25ms slices with no idle waits; small restores publish in the same task.
  - Session registration batched (`IAgentHostConnectionsService.batchSessionResolutionChanges`), plus an indexed `findSessionResource`.
  - Session list rows no longer hydrate drafts, so they don't subscribe to full default-chat snapshots.
- **Correctness follow-ups**
  - Draft rehydration after reconnect.
  - Completed-turn seeding by id.
  - Path cache carried across rebuilds.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Behavior changes**
  - Progress bar appears after 100ms.
  - Chat view is reused on session switch.
  - Pills fill in progressively.
  - Non-visible sessions do not restore their draft agent/model until shown or queried.
  - `IChatViewModel.getItems()` returns a readonly array.
  - New platform method `batchSessionResolutionChanges` is client-only, with no protocol change.
- **Known follow-ups (pre-existing, not in this PR)**
  - 1.09s task for the visible 71MB snapshot (AHP JSONL logger re-stringify plus `turnsToHistory`).
  - Checkpoint lookup on publish.
  - Unchanged sessions updated on refresh.
  - Duplicate concurrent chat subscribes.
  - AHP subscribe churn / PR-operation advertisement storm in the agent host.
- **Review process:** every change had an independent review, plus two full-branch reviews. A renderer hang found during manual testing was fixed with a regression test.

## Validation

- `npm run install-fast`: passed
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only`: passed
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run <14 chat/sessions/agentHost test files>`: 2538 passing, 0 failing
- Hygiene: passed (commit pre-commit hook, on the merge and follow-up commits)

The merge of `origin/main` had three conflicts (`baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts`, `agentHostSessionInputPills.test.ts`, `chatService.test.ts`), resolved by keeping both sides. Chat view test fakes were updated for new `main` fields.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Hot scrolling and rendering callers repeatedly invoked getItems(), and each invocation allocated and scanned the entire transcript.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: A 1,157-request chat spent about 3.6 seconds per scrollbar drag in getItems/isHiddenFromTranscript scans, contributing to renderer freezes.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Returns one cached readonly visible-items array until a model or response change invalidates it, removing transcript-wide scans from repeated scroll/render queries.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Before the PR, every getItems() call rebuilt the visible transcript by filtering the full _items array and computing pending/divider state. The changed implementation caches that result at RIGHT line 387 and invalidates it on model/view-model changes. The PR's traced large-chat scrollbar scenario reports getItems/isHiddenFromTranscript scanning falling from 3.6s per drag to under 1ms, and the added test verifies repeated reads perform one pending-request scan independent of call count.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Each rendered request row immediately read bounding rectangles after render writes, forcing repeated synchronous layout during scrolling and rerendering.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Dragging the scrollbar in a 1,157-request chat produced repeated long tasks and several seconds of sticky-scroll/layout CPU.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Defers request-row geometry reads to one coalesced per-frame pass and refreshes sticky scroll only after ranges are measured.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The base code measured sticky-scroll source geometry synchronously from each request-row render. RIGHT line 1982 now schedules one shared source-range pass, and the new scheduler measures all rendered rows after writes once per animation frame. Tests verify zero geometry reads during row render and one measurement per row in the frame. The PR trace reports sticky-scroll drag CPU dropping from 5.2s to 0.57s and long tasks from 170 to 40.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Rendering passive session-list metadata eagerly subscribed to each session's full default-chat snapshot, transferring and processing large transcripts that were not open.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: On reload, list rows pulled a 71MB default-chat snapshot and spent about 704ms on data that the visible workflow did not need.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Passive list-row reads retain only the lightweight session-state subscription; default-chat draft hydration is started lazily for visible or explicitly queried sessions and restored on reconnect.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base revision, opening a session-state subscription unconditionally called _whenBackendDefaultChat and hydrated the draft agent/model, which subscribes to the default chat snapshot. The PR changes passive session-list reference paths to call _ensureSessionStateSubscription(sessionId, false) and tracks hydration separately; tests show list rows subscribe only to session state while the visible/explicit session alone subscribes to its default chat. The supplied user trace identifies a 71MB default-chat snapshot pulled by list rows for 704ms.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or switch to a large Agent Host chat with roughly 1,157 completed requests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The selected chat must acquire/restore its model and attach it to the chat widget before the transcript is usable. Remote history replay now runs in bounded 25ms macrotask slices; completed-turn customization parsing is scheduled off the selection task and is not on the initial-render critical path. A reused single-group ChatView avoids widget reconstruction, and loading feedback begins after 100ms.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe to Agent Host session/chat state snapshots consumed by the selected chat's output observables.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One session-state subscription plus one chat-state subscription for the active observed chat; reference counting can share an already-open wire subscription.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same snapshots were subscribed, then the full transcript's customization references were parsed and resolved synchronously when selected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The active chat snapshot is required, but the PR does not add the subscription. Customization projection is moved after receipt and off the click task.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Scan response parts/tool input strings and resolve customization path references.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Completed turns are processed once in 8ms idle slices, with per-turn and per-path caches; the active turn is processed per streaming state update as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All completed turns and the active turn were projected synchronously on the selection/read task; active-turn reparsing already occurred per update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completed history is off the open critical path; only the current active turn remains synchronous.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Completed turn count and response-part/path-token count; the reviewed trace uses 1,157 requests. Effective work is reduced by per-turn parsing, path-token caching, and one active observed chat.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One CooperativeMutationBudget serializes each chat's history mutations across macrotasks. There is no new shared cross-chat limiter, but the reviewed product path loads the selected chat; customization work is one cancellable idle job per observed chat and each job processes turns serially.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold open progressively fills per-turn results and the customization index's positive/negative path cache. Equivalent customization/root snapshots retain the index and path results; a chat/host scope change drops per-turn scope state. Warm reads reuse the ChatView, visible-item array, response request-index hints, and resolved customization paths.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed call paths and tests directly establish deferred customization work, bounded replay slices, view reuse, and cache invalidation behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact distribution of response-part sizes and concurrent chat restores varies, but the changed critical-path placement and bounded scheduling are directly evidenced. The immediate same-task publish applies only when replay took under 10ms and never yielded; no concrete regressive render cost was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff removes synchronous transcript-wide work and view reconstruction; possible tradeoffs such as immediate publication for sub-10ms replay are bounded and do not establish a realistic net degradation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Drag or scroll through a very large rendered transcript with sticky scroll enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each animation frame must render/recycle visible rows, establish sticky source ranges, refresh sticky state, and paint. Geometry measurement is now deferred until row writes finish and coalesced into one pass in the current/next frame.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read request/row/sticky DOM bounding rectangles, potentially crossing the browser layout boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one batched pass per frame, reading each currently rendered request/sticky row once; row render calls only upgrade/share that pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each request render synchronously measured its own source range, and later refreshes could repeat collection-wide geometry work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The batched read remains on the frame path but replaces one synchronous measurement per row render and avoids read/write interleaving.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of currently rendered request rows and scroll/render frames, not the full 1,157-item transcript after tree virtualization.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A MutableDisposable permits one pending source-range pass. Requests raised during a running refresh are deferred to the next frame, preventing same-frame recursive measurement; state refresh is likewise coalesced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Measured ranges and width ratios are cached by request id and deleted when templates/view models are removed. Unchanged ranges do not trigger another sticky refresh; disposal cancels pending passes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed scheduling, range comparison, cleanup paths, and animation-frame tests prove cardinality and lifecycle.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser layout cost depends on row complexity and viewport size, but tests and supplied traces directly establish the prior forced-layout mechanism and per-frame coalescing.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new pass reduces synchronous layout work and explicitly settles after refresh-driven rerenders.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reload the window and register/render a list containing tens of Agent Host sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The host session catalog must be applied, frontend resources registered, dependent session resolution updated, and visible list metadata published. Full default-chat snapshots are not required for passive rows and are now deferred until a session is visible or explicitly queried.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe over the Agent Host connection to session state and, when requested, the default chat snapshot used to hydrate draft agent/model state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Passive list rows retain one lightweight session-state subscription per referenced session but zero default-chat subscriptions; only visible or explicit sessions add their default-chat snapshot subscription. Reference counting shares duplicate consumers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every session-state subscription immediately hydrated the default draft and therefore subscribed to the full default-chat snapshot, including non-visible sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Session metadata remains required for list rows; potentially very large default-chat snapshots are removed from the passive-list reload critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Notify all session-resolution observers and resolve backend-to-frontend session identities.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One notification per bulk refresh rather than one per newly registered session; warm and cold identity lookups are one Map lookup after registration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each of N new registrations fired a global resolution event, and findSessionResource linearly scanned all registered resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The single notification remains on the registration critical path but avoids N observer recomputations as the list grows.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Listed session count (the added bulk test uses 60) and default-chat snapshot size (the supplied trace includes 71MB). Effective notification cardinality is one per refresh; default-chat snapshot cardinality is visible/explicit sessions only.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Session registration remains a synchronous loop but resolution notifications are nested-safe batched into one event. Session-state subscriptions are reference-counted; default-chat hydration is one-shot per active subscription store and reconnect recreates it only for sessions whose hydration was requested.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Backend identity mappings are populated during registration and serve O(1) warm lookups. Session subscriptions survive short passive gaps via existing idle retention; hydration-request flags are removed when subscriptions expire or sessions are deleted and reapplied after reconnect.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the batch implementation, provider call site, subscription gate, and tests directly prove the changed fan-out and wire-subscription behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalog sizes and snapshot bytes differ by user, but boundary cardinality and removal of passive full-chat hydration are explicit and covered by reconnect/list-row tests.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff removes an N-event recomputation storm and avoids eager per-row full-chat snapshot transfers without adding a new scaling boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Switch repeatedly between single-group sessions and update chat renderer options while detached or zero-height
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing ChatGroupView is reattached, rebound to the next session/chat model, laid out, and any pending list rerender is flushed only once the list has nonzero connected dimensions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read DOM connection/height and rerender list rows when layout dimensions are valid.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One offsetHeight check per renderer-option/style transition while visible; detached requests collapse into one rerender on the next layout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Visible widgets rerendered immediately even when their list DOM was detached or measured zero height, and session switches disposed/recreated the entire chat view.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A connected visible update still rerenders immediately; detached/zero-height reconstruction is moved off the invalid layout state and flushed after layout.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Session-switch frequency and rendered row count. Reuse is limited to one outgoing single-group view, so retained UI state does not grow with switch history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Session switches are synchronous and ownership is transferred to exactly one disposable store. Rerender demand is represented by one boolean, so multiple detached updates coalesce into one post-layout rerender.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Exactly one ChatGroupView is reused when both sessions have one group; restored multi-group layouts reject and dispose it. Pending rerender state is cleared before a successful rerender and does not accumulate.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for ownership, coalescing, and call frequency based on changed conditions and lifecycle tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact widget-construction and offsetHeight costs depend on transcript complexity, but reuse is constant-space and the added geometry read occurs only on low-frequency option transitions, not per scroll frame.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The one-view cache is bounded and disposal paths are covered; the new height check prevents the demonstrated zero-height rerender loop rather than moving work onto a hotter path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 32 changed files and relevant callers/tests. The PR is a performance-fix series: it coalesces registration and sticky-layout work, caches repeated transcript queries, defers transcript-wide customization processing, bounds history replay, reuses one chat view, and removes eager default-chat snapshot hydration for passive rows. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue met the reporting threshold; three concrete shipped regression fixes were recorded for internal learning.
